interpretation: Exact edge-flux residuals reject both stored local iterates; evaluator rounding cannot explain the misses.
Each final repair epoch has one update. Its exact anchor-plus-rounded-product sum passes the unchanged captured target; flattening reproduces the original failing vector bit for bit.
Whole-trajectory re-summing also changes old rounding errors to which subsequent residual replacements already responded. Its worse residuals are not evidence against a live compensated recurrence.

The unflattened passing vectors are diagnostics only. No acceptable flattened fix, universal binary64 floor, coefficient forward-error bound, production regression failure, or cross-platform vector identity is established.
